newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen easing further after Dow's slip.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen easing further after Dow's slip.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to consolidate further on Thursday, as the steep fall on Wall Street will make market participants who have hoped for continued buying by overseas investors cautious, brokers said.
On Wednesday, the 225-share Nikkei average fell 132.02 points, or 0.65 percent, to 20,048.90. Its June futures slipped 110 points to 20,080.
"The market is likely to remain in an adjustment phase today," said Seiki Orimi, analyst at Dai-Ichi Securities Co.
The Nikkei 225 average retreated on Wednesday, mostly on profit taking, after a five-day winning streak.
Orimi said caution over the fast pace of the Nikkei's recent gains grew on Tuesday when the index surged and deviated from its 25-day moving average by nearly 10 percent.
Brokers said position adjustments would be further prompted by the steepest loss in U.S. stocks in nearly a month on Wednesday.
The Dow industrials tumbled 140 points to close at 7,086, hit by a sharp rise in interest rates. The loss was the Dow's biggest since April 11.
In other indices, the broader TOPIX index gave up 5.96 points or 0.40 percent to 1,494.56, and the Nikkei 300 average eased 1.27 points or 0.44 percent to 290.67.
Stocks opened weaker, following U.S. stocks' sharp fall.

But investors sought blue-chip issues, whose rises had relatively lagged behind, including Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd and Yamanouchi Pharmaceutical Co Ltd.

Shares in Tokio Marine, a major casualty insurance firm, gained 30 yen to 1,400 by midday. Its turnover of 3.875 million shares was the second-heaviest on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Yamanouchi jumped 100 yen to 2,970 by midday, with turnover of 1.529 million shares.

Share of Sony hit a record high of 9,800 yen in the morning, lifted by early buying on expectations of a solid earnings report due out 0600 GMT. Sony stood 120 yen higher at 9,750 at midday. Its turnover of 1.8616 million shares was ninth heaviest.

By sector, decliners were led by real estate, rubber, brokerages, banks and ceramics. The major advancing sectors were services, land transport, miscellaneous manufacturing, fisheries and pharmaceuticals.
